This page explains the **low-altitude economy** in simple English. Use it before the week pages under **Teach**.

Harder words and legal names appear here too. When you see a new term, this page says what it means the first time. Longer definitions sit in the [Glossary](glossary.qmd). Checked programme facts sit on [Official status](tracker.qmd).

## A whole service, not only a vehicle

In Hong Kong, the **low-altitude economy (LAE)** means business and other paid activity that uses airspace generally below about **1,000 metres**.

That **1,000 metre** figure is a **policy working description** — a way officials and analysts talk about the field. It is **not** the same thing as a flying-height limit in Hong Kong’s main drone law, Cap. 448G ([Glossary · altitude scale](glossary.qmd#altitude-scale); [Official status](tracker.qmd)).

Think of one finished job, not only one aircraft:

- Someone needs a delivery, an inspection, a medical transfer, or a similar task.
- An **operator** flies the aircraft or runs the flight.
- The aircraft needs a place to take off and land.
- Someone helps coordinate traffic and communications.
- **Customers** (or **mission sponsors**) pay for the result.
- Other firms support the work — for example finance, insurance, training, and software platforms.

That whole chain is what this course means by LAE. [Week 1](week-01.qmd) starts the same idea. The week map is on [Course overview](overview.qmd).

On the Mainland, **低空经济** (low-altitude economy) uses a **different** statistical and industrial-policy scope (NDRC 发改低空〔2025〕1676号). Do **not** treat that Mainland measure as the same number as a Hong Kong **value-added** figure ([Glossary](glossary.qmd#mainland-comparators); [Official status](tracker.qmd)).

## Labels you will meet (keep light)

You will hear everyday words (such as “drone”) next to law or industry labels. Keep them separate.

- **Small unmanned aircraft (SUA)** — Hong Kong’s main legal label for light unmanned craft under [Cap. 448G](glossary.qmd#hong-kong-institutions-and-law). Cap. 448G covers unmanned aircraft **not more than 150 kg**. “Drone” in everyday speech is **not** a Cap. 448G legal synonym.
- **eVTOL** — an industry label for **electric vertical take-off and landing** craft (aircraft that take off and land straight up and down, usually with electric power). Hong Kong has **no dedicated eVTOL statute yet**. Heavier or passenger types sit above the SUA weight ceiling. They are treated as **unconventional aircraft** while rules are still being developed ([Glossary · vehicles](glossary.qmd#vehicles-and-operations); [Official status](tracker.qmd)).

```{=html}
  <text x="581" y="98" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#C5A572">eVTOL</text>
  <text x="581" y="124" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="700" fill="#003366">Electric VTOL</text>
  <text x="581" y="144" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="700" fill="#003366">(industry)</text>
  <text x="581" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#1a1a1a">Not a Cap. 448G</text>
  <text x="581" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#1a1a1a">synonym for SUA</text>
  <text x="581" y="214" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#5f5f5f">Often heavier types</text>

  <rect x="60" y="254" width="600" height="70" rx="8" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#C5A572" stroke-width="2"/>

  <text x="360" y="304" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,Segoe UI,sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#5f5f5f">U-space ≠ HK law · Sandbox ≠ Sandbox X · Glossary for the rest</text>

</svg>
<p class="wdiag-note">From primer labels. SVG upgrade of HTML #lae-labels. Mild overlap with Week 1 nested labels — keep light.</p>

```

A few more labels you will see in readings:

- **Vertiport** — industry word for a take-off and landing site for advanced craft. Hong Kong has **no dedicated vertiport statute yet** ([Glossary · infrastructure](glossary.qmd#infrastructure)).
- **U-space** — an EU / industry traffic concept. **U-space is not Hong Kong law.**
- **UTM** — **unmanned aircraft system traffic management**; industry usage for digital traffic coordination.
- Hong Kong’s **Smart Low-altitude Traffic Management System** is **planned** (Policy Address language: progressive implementation from **2028**). It is **not** a statute yet ([Glossary · airspace](glossary.qmd#airspace-and-traffic); [Timeline](dates.qmd)).

Weight ladders, **BVLOS** (**beyond visual line of sight** — flying when the remote pilot cannot see the aircraft), and permission diagrams live on the Glossary. This page does not reprint them.

## Why Hong Kong and the GBA

This course focuses on **Hong Kong** and the **Greater Bay Area (GBA)** — the city cluster that includes Hong Kong, Macao, and nearby Guangdong cities.

Readings also use EU, US, and NASA-style examples for **comparison**. Those foreign frames are **not** Hong Kong law. See [Course overview](overview.qmd) and the week pages under **Teach**.

Hong Kong already has an active policy track: a Working Group, trial programmes (**sandboxes**), Cap. 448G, and Advisory Circulars. The dated trail is on [Timeline](dates.qmd).
